text: All leads (L1 through L8) were verified and confirmed as genuine security issues or security misconfigurations in Dockerfile and app.py.

findings.title: Missing non-root USER in Dockerfile
findings.explanation: The Dockerfile does not specify a non-root USER instruction. Consequently, the container runs processes as the root user by default, increasing the attack surface and potential impact if the container is compromised.
findings.fix: Add a non-root user and switch to it using USER before CMD/ENTRYPOINT.
findings.description: The Dockerfile does not specify a non-root USER instruction. Consequently, the container runs processes as the root user by default, increasing the attack surface and potential impact if the container is compromised.
findings.code:
FROM python:3.9-alpine

WORKDIR /app

RUN apk add --no-cache bind-tools

COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

COPY . .

EXPOSE 5013

CMD ["python", "app.py"]

findings.title: Remote Command Injection via subprocess with shell=True
findings.explanation: User input from request.form.get('domain') is passed directly into a shell command string and executed via subprocess.Popen with shell=True, allowing arbitrary command injection.
findings.fix: Avoid shell=True and pass arguments as a list (e.g., ['dig', domain]), or strictly validate and sanitize user input.
findings.description: User input from request.form.get('domain') is passed directly into a shell command string and executed via subprocess.Popen with shell=True, allowing arbitrary command injection.

findings.title: Arbitrary Code Execution via eval()
findings.explanation: Untrusted user input from request.form.get('val') is passed directly into Python's built-in eval() function, allowing arbitrary Python code execution.
findings.fix: Avoid using eval() on untrusted user input. Use a safe expression evaluator or parse the input safely.
findings.description: Untrusted user input from request.form.get('val') is passed directly into Python's built-in eval() function, allowing arbitrary Python code execution.

findings.title: Flask Debug Mode Enabled and Bound to All Interfaces
findings.explanation: Running Flask with debug=True enables the interactive debugger and exposes sensitive information or allows code execution in error pages. Binding to 0.0.0.0 exposes the server to all network interfaces.
findings.fix: Disable debug mode in production (debug=False) and restrict host binding as necessary.
